title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Abstract supports dominant HMN due to heterozygous SPTAN1 (nonsense) mutations; HMND11 label is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene encodes alpha-II spectrin.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: SPTAN1 is identified as the alpha-II spectrin gene.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is an autosomal dominant inherited peripheral neuropathy with juvenile onset. It is marked by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons. Penetrance is variable, and severity differs greatly between patients (Beijer et al., 2019).

checks.explanation: Combined with the three dominant families, this supports an autosomal dominant inherited peripheral neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to identify heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene in affected members of 3 unrelated families with dominant hereditary motor neuropathy. Mutant mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was broken down by nonsense-mediated decay, and protein levels in patient cells were reduced. The authors noted that dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations had been described earlier as causing a range of epilepsy phenotypes.
